subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: May core expose an opt-in timeout that releases a session while a non-cooperative ContextEngine.maintain() continues in the background, with fencing limited to host-owned transcript and task-state writes?
rationale: Source review can establish that the proposed fencing is internally coherent, but only context-engine owners can define whether abandoned plugin execution, a new config key, and a generic queue timeout callback are acceptable permanent contracts.

options.title: Approve opt-in abandonment
options.body: Keep the disabled-by-default setting, document the host/plugin side-effect boundary, resolve conflicts, and validate the refreshed exact head before merge.

options.title: Require cooperative cancellation
options.body: Pause this PR until the context-engine lifecycle provides an owner-approved cancellation signal and plugins can stop work before the lane is released.

options.title: Decline new surface
options.body: Close or substantially narrow the PR if owners prefer existing session recovery and plugin-level lock management over another core config and queue callback.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in abandonment
recommendation.body: Keep the disabled-by-default setting, document the host/plugin side-effect boundary, resolve conflicts, and validate the refreshed exact head before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history points to this person as the introducer of deferred background maintenance and the strongest available owner for its permanent timeout semantics.
